"I want you to create a game about being a gritty, hard-boiled 1940s noir detective solving randomized murder mysteries late at night. 

Here is how the game works and what you need to build:
- Visuals @COMMENT_BODY@ Atmosphere: Dark, moody noir aesthetic with rain, shadows, and dramatic lighting. Keep all text descriptions short, punchy, and under two sentences—no long paragraphs.
- Randomized Cases: Every time a new game starts, randomly generate a new Victim, a Murder Weapon, 3 Suspects (with motives and alibis), 4 Clues (including 1 definitive \"Smoking Gun\" clue that proves who did it), and 1 True Killer.
- Stage 1 - The Call: Start the game in a dark detective office with a rotary phone ringing at 2:00 AM. Give the player the crime scene address and a short tip from Sergeant Miller, with a button to [Head to the Crime Scene].
- Stage 2 - Top-Down Crime Scene: Show a top-down view of the crime scene room with 4 clickable/tappable objects (such as a desk, a shattered window, a coat, or a safe).
- Stage 3 - The Zoom-In: When the player taps an object, zoom in to a detailed close-up view of that object and reveal one clue with a single gritty sentence describing what was found. Include a button to [Zoom Out].
- Stage 4 - The Evidence Board: Always show a button to [Open Evidence Board]. On the Evidence Board screen, display all clues discovered so far, profile cards for the 3 suspects, and buttons to [Accuse a Suspect] or [Return to Crime Scene].
- Win/Loss Conditions: If the player accuses the wrong suspect, or tries to accuse the right suspect without having found the \"Smoking Gun\" clue first, trigger a Game Over screen where the killer escapes and the case goes cold. If the player finds the \"Smoking Gun\" and accuses the true killer, trigger a Victory screen where the killer is arrested.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')

Empty HTML project. I'll build a single-page static game with vanilla JS/CSS. Rich noir atmosphere with CSS/SVG art. Need randomized cases with 4 clues, one smoking gun, 3 suspects, evidence board, stages.

"Visuals @COMMENT_BODY@" — likely a bad substitution but implies visuals matter. Let's aim for a high-quality, atmospheric game: rain animation, film grain, vignette, top-down room illustration via SVG, close-up object illustrations via SVG, evidence board with pinned cards, typewriter fonts, dramatic lighting. All offline (no external fonts maybe could use Google Fonts but better to avoid network dependencies; use serif stacks + maybe embed fonts? Use system fonts with letterspacing. Could import Google Fonts but preview may have network. Better self-contained: use font stacks like "Courier New", Georgia. Might use Google Fonts but risky. I'll use local stacks and CSS effects.

Let's design carefully.

Game architecture:
- index.html, styles.css, game.js, maybe art.js for SVG generation.
- Procedural case generator with handcrafted data pools that guarantee coherence: 4 objects each tied to a clue. One clue is smoking gun directly proving killer. Templates need to work for any suspect. Better approach: generate victim, weapon, 3 suspects with motive/alibi, and 4 clues:
  - clue 1 (object A) atmospheric/motive-related, points weakly to a suspect
  - clue 2 (object B) alibi contradiction
  - clue 3 (object C) physical evidence tying to killer
  - clue 4 smoking gun explicit (e.g., matching fingerprint/ blood-stained cufflink) proving killer.
Need randomized each new game. Clues include suspect reference; description single gritty sentence (< 2 sentences). Ensure smoking gun is truly definitive: mention suspect name and evidence.

Simplify coherently: Generate killer among 3. Then for each object, generate clue content based on templates and roles. Clues should be discoverable in any order. Evidence board shows profiles and clues discovered so far, with locked placeholders.

Stages:
1. Office: rotary phone ringing 2:00 AM. Address and tip from Sgt Miller, button [Head to the Crime Scene]. Could animate phone ringing + rain through blinds. Nice SVG/CSS art.
2. Crime scene top-down room with 4 clickable objects: desk, shattered window, coat, safe. Use CSS-positioned SVG objects with hotspots and labels. Maybe room floor rendered SVG perspective top-down with furniture; highlight on hover.
3. Zoom-in: big illustration of object, clue reveal, [Zoom Out], plus [Open Evidence Board] persistent.
4. Evidence board: clues found, suspect profile cards, buttons [Accuse a Suspect] and [Return to Crime Scene]. Accuse opens suspect selection perhaps modal, or cards with accuse buttons. Must have buttons to accuse. I'll include an "Accuse" mode: click [Accuse a Suspect] to reveal accusation controls on each suspect card, then confirm.
- Win/loss screens. Loss if wrong suspect or no smoking gun. Victory if right with smoking gun.
- New case / Play again resets with randomization.

Extra polish: sound? Could add WebAudio ambient rain and phone ring toggle. Maybe subtle. Autoplay restrictions; add sound toggle. Nice-to-have. Could add typewriter text effect. Keep text short.

Also mobile responsive.

Visual atmosphere:
- color palette: near black #07080a, warm amber #e0a54b, cold blue #7f9bb3, blood red #a33127.
- Film grain overlay via SVG feTurbulence data URI, animated.
- Rain streaks via CSS pseudo elements / canvas? Use a canvas rain layer with requestAnimationFrame for background (lightweight), or CSS repeating linear gradients animated. Canvas gives better look. Use fixed canvas with rain streaks and occasional lightning? Noir city. But screens have varied backgrounds. A full-screen rain canvas overlay behind UI with opacity, plus window rain in office scene. Could do CSS rain (two layers of thin diagonal white lines) with animation.

- Office scene: SVG illustration: window with venetian blinds and rain, desk lamp pool of light, rotary phone on desk, silhouette detective? Could draw with SVG + gradients. Keep stylish. I can craft nice SVG: office wall, window, blinds, rain lines, desk, phone with ringing animation, cigarette smoke, lamp. Use CSS transforms for phone shake and sound rings.
- Crime scene: SVG top-down floor plan: room rectangle, rug, desk, window, coat rack with coat, safe, chalk outline of victim. 4 hotspots. Use glow ring markers numbered 1-4 perhaps. Hover labels.
- Close-up art per object: inline SVG illustrations for desk, window, coat, safe. Each rendered in zoom screen, with a spotlight gradient. Draw distinct art using SVG.
- Evidence board: corkboard texture, red string connecting items, paper cards with pushpins, typewriter font. Suspect photos: stylized noir portrait SVG silhouettes (fedora, cigarette, veil). Procedural portraits maybe based on 3 archetypes.

Suspect generation: pools of names, occupations, motives, alibis, portrait style. Need 3 suspects each with motive and alibi. Motive should relate to victim. Alibi should be specific. Randomize.

Case generation:
- Victim: name, occupation/descriptor, cause? Weapon.
- Addresses: e.g., "221 Ashcombe Street, Room 4B", "The Nightingale Hotel, Suite 12". Tip from Miller referencing address and suspect/detail.
